question: How can an open video generator be evolved into a real-time, action-controllable, minute-long-memory world simulator, and released openly?
hypothesis: A staged pipeline (video prior, long-sequence action-conditioned middle-training, causal few-step distillation) yields a high-fidelity, high-dynamics, real-time open world model.
contributions: A scalable data engine with hierarchical (narrative, scene-static, dense temporal) captions over real, game and Unreal Engine data
A multi-stage pipeline: pre-training, middle-training (MoE, 5s to 60s curriculum, action adapters), post-training (block causal attention, DMD distillation)
Applications: promptable world events, an action agent, 3D reconstruction; code and weights released

method.summary: Starts from the 14B Wan2.2 image-to-video MoE diffusion model (two 14B experts, 28B total), trains it on progressively longer clips (5s to 60s) with image-to-video and video-to-video tasks, then freezes the DiT and finetunes action adapters (Plucker camera embeddings plus multi-hot keys via AdaLN). Post-training makes a causal block-attention student from the high-noise expert and distils it with DMD, self-rollout and an adversarial head into LingBot-World-Fast.

datasets.name: General video corpus (first- and third-person videos of humans, animals, vehicles; in-house and open-source)
datasets.preprocessing: filter by resolution and duration; clip slicing with Koala and TransNet v2; VLM scoring of quality, motion magnitude, scene perspective; MegaSAM pseudo camera poses; hierarchical captions

datasets.name: Game data
datasets.source: own capture platform; RGB paired with keyboard inputs and camera parameters
datasets.preprocessing: no UI overlays; timestamped control signals

datasets.name: Unreal Engine synthetic data
datasets.preprocessing: collision-checked procedural or imported real-world camera trajectories with ground-truth intrinsics and extrinsics

datasets.name: Curated VBench test set of generated videos
datasets.size: 100 generated videos, each longer than 30 seconds

models.name: LingBot-World-Base (middle-trained)
models.params: 28B total (two experts of about 14B, one active per timestep)
models.architecture: bidirectional MoE DiT with high-noise and low-noise experts, self-attn, AdaLN action injection, cross-attn on text
models.context: clips up to 60 s in training; samples up to 10 min shown

models.name: LingBot-World-Fast (post-trained)
models.architecture: block causal attention with KV cache, few-step distilled

other.speed: 16 fps at 480p on one GPU node

other.output: actions for next 10 seconds: W A S D and I J K L

training.objective: Eq 1 maximise log p(x_{t:t+L} | x_<t, a_{t:t+L}) (diffusion); causal stage: Eq 2 regression to clean x0 at selected timesteps with diffusion forcing; DMD loss (Eq 4) plus adversarial softplus loss on a discriminator head (Eq 5-6)
training.seq_len: 5 s clips, progressively extended to 60 s
training.regularisation: no R1/R2 in the adversarial objective

other.flow_shift: scaled up progressively with video duration
other.action_finetune: freeze main DiT blocks, train only action adapters (embedding projections and AdaLN)
other.distillation: real score = middle-trained MoE teacher; fake score initialised from same teacher; two-time-scale updates; gradient truncated to last K steps (K not given); timestep 0 sampling added; target timesteps {t1..tm} not given
other.student_init: high-noise expert, chosen over low-noise by an unreported experiment

inference.decoding: autoregressive chunked generation with KV cache (Fast); few denoising steps (number not stated)
inference.prompting: text prompts for promptable events; image or video as initial state

metrics.name: VBench Imaging Quality, Aesthetic Quality, Dynamic Degree, Motion Smoothness, Temporal Flickering, Overall Consistency

eval.protocol: 100 generated videos over 30 s; which variant (Base or Fast) was scored is not stated; single run, no significance test

evidence.quote: Running the model requires enterprise-grade GPUs
evidence.where: 6.2 Limitations (inference cost; training compute not stated)

results.claim: LingBot-World scores highest on VBench dynamic degree, versus Yume-1.5 and HY-World 1.5.
results.setup: VBench on 100 generated videos each over 30 s; variant scored not stated
results.quote: achieving a score of 0.8857 compared to 0.7612 for Yume-1.5 and 0.7217 for HY-World 1.5

results.claim: LingBot-World has the best imaging quality of the three.
results.table: Table 2, row Ours, column Imaging Quality

results.claim: Motion smoothness and temporal flickering are below HY-World 1.5 but above Yume-1.5.
results.setup: same as above; motion smoothness 0.9895 ours vs 0.9897 HY-World, 0.9709 Yume
results.table: Table 2, row Ours, column Temporal Flickering

results.claim: Real-time variant runs at 16 fps at 480p with under 1 s latency.
results.setup: LingBot-World-Fast, 480p, one GPU node; no GPU model named
results.quote: which achieves 16 fps throughput when processing 480p videos on a system with one GPU node

results.claim: Coherent video up to ten minutes is shown qualitatively; landmarks persist after 60 s out of view.

limits: Memory is emergent from the context window, with no explicit module; unstable over long simulation
Action space limited to navigation; no object-level grounding; single agent only
Generation length limited and scenes drift
Quantitative evaluation is VBench only, two baselines, no comparison with Genie 3 or Mirage 2 (closed), and the scored variant is not stated
Training hyperparameters, data sizes and compute are not reported
